A **(plane) projective curve** is a closed subset $C=V(F)\subseteq\mathbf P^2$ given by a nonconstant square-free homogeneous form $F\in k[x_0,x_1,x_2]$ [[def-homogeneous-polynomial-and-homogeneous-ideal]], [[def-projective-algebraic-set]], [[thm-projective-zariski-topology]]. Its **degree** is $\deg F$ [[def-polynomial-degree-leading-coefficient-and-monic]], and its **irreducible components** are the closed sets $V(h)$ for the distinct irreducible factors $h$ of $F$, each taken once. Thus every component is reduced and occurs with multiplicity one, $C$ may be reducible, and $C$ is nonempty.
